name: Macbeth
tagline: The Hero Devoured by His Own Ambition
public_profile: The real murderer who killed King Duncan with his own hands.
case_background: King Duncan of Scotland has died mysteriously in the castle of Macbeth—the general he trusted most. Was it sudden illness, or murder? On the night before Macbeth's coronation, five people who hold the fate of the kingdom gather together. You must find the truth, and decide who will wear the crown.

case_details.label: Victim
case_details.value: King Duncan

case_details.label: Crime Scene
case_details.value: The king was stabbed through the heart with a dagger. The blade was coated with a rare snake poison: the wound turned black and the blood would not clot.

case_details.label: Time of Death
case_details.value: Between 11 p.m. and 1 a.m.

case_details.label: Place
case_details.value: In the guest room of Macbeth's castle.

core_rules: Stay in character at all times.
Try to complete your public goal and secret missions. Guess other players' secret missions—and stop them.
You may lie, but only in character.
goals: Claim that you are the best choice to steady the kingdom and inherit the throne.
Lead everyone to believe the witches' prophecy recognizes your right to be king.
secrets: Hide the fact that you are Duncan's murderer.
Hide the fact that Lady Macbeth was your partner in the crime.
Find out who might be the man 'not born of woman'—and watch him carefully.
story: You are a hero of great military fame, King Duncan's own cousin. He trusted you deeply, and not long ago gave you the title of the Thane of Cawdor.

The witches' prophecy woke up your ambition for the throne. Together with your wife, you conspired to plan and carry out the murder. After the guards were drugged and fell asleep, you stabbed the king to death with a poisoned dagger—with your own hands.
Your wife helped you fake the crime scene: she pushed the murder weapon into the hand of a drugged guard.
You are the murderer in this case. You must act like a grieving hero, and turn all suspicion toward others. You are the only person who knows all of Lady Macbeth's crimes.
initial_information: Macduff's close relative once started a rebellion. You and Banquo crushed it. To show a king's 'mercy' and to calm the Fife family, Duncan forgave Macduff and let him keep his title.
You and Banquo both won great battles, but only you received a new title.
Malcolm disagreed with his father Duncan about politics.
Hail, Macbeth! Future king!
You shall never be king, but your sons shall rule the land.
No man born of woman can harm Macbeth.
Macbeth shall never be defeated, until the forest of Birnam marches toward Dunsinane Hill.

timeline.description: You and Banquo met three witches on the heath and heard their prophecy. Deeply shaken, you wrote a letter to your wife about it.
After your victorious return, Banquo stayed at your castle as a guest. The prophecy began to spread through the kingdom. Then King Duncan announced he would visit your castle and stay the night.
King Duncan returned to the east guest room, escorted by the royal guards—Malcolm's own men. Macbeth's soldiers guarded the outer walls.

After the king left, you saw Banquo and Macduff talking. Busy with your own plan, you did not stay to listen, and soon both men went back to their rooms. A handwritten, unsent note was later found among Banquo's things: 'I, Banquo, have a matter touching the kingdom's safety. I beg a meeting at midnight in the east-wing side hall.'

Lady Macbeth, saying 'the king needs rest', ordered her trusted maid to bring strong poppy juice from the cellar. She mixed it into the wine sent to the king's guards. The guards drank and fell into a deep sleep.

Torn by your inner struggle, you walked up and down the east corridor. Twenty minutes later you met Banquo, who also looked troubled. You exchanged a few words about the three weird sisters, then you went back to your room first.
Your wife confirmed the guards were drugged and gave you the signal. You slipped into the king's bedroom and stabbed the sleeping Duncan with the poisoned dagger. You took the weapon away with you.

Macduff, as master of ceremonies, went with you to wake the king—and found him dead. His cry woke the whole castle. An unconscious guard held a bloody dagger and was beginning to wake. Malcolm's royal guards had disappeared. A silver ring bearing the crest of the Fife family was found on the guard.

story: You are Macbeth's wife, and a subject of the king. King Duncan is an honored guest under your own roof.
You have a strong desire for power and control, and a burning ambition to become queen. You think Macbeth is 'too soft', and that he needs your push.
It was you who drugged the guards.
After Macbeth killed the king and came back in a panic, it was you who calmly took the dagger back to the crime scene and framed the guard.
The king's blood stained the sleeve of your fine dress.

The House of Macduff has long-standing grievances against the royal house.
Banquo knows of the prophecies and has acquiesced to your plot. He is a double-edged sword and must be handled with caution.

story: You are a loyal general of the kingdom, and Macbeth's comrade-in-arms.
In crushing the rebellion and helping Duncan take the throne, your deeds were equal to Macbeth's—if not greater.

Yet at the victory feast, Duncan heaped titles on Macbeth alone—the new Thane of Cawdor—while your deeds received no more than a passing word of praise. His reason: 'Banquo's loyalty needs no title to prove it.'
The witches also prophesied that your descendants would be kings. This leaves you with mixed feelings—jealousy, perhaps, or fear.
On the night of the murder, you tried to send King Duncan a secret warning, but you failed.

story: You are Duncan's eldest son, first in line to the throne.

You are a radical reformer: you think your father ruled too 'softly', while Duncan thought you 'rash and reckless', a danger to the kingdom's stability. Again and again he struck down your proposals at court, and even let slip words like 'Macbeth reminds me of my younger self' or 'Banquo's loyalty is more reassuring'. You resented every word of it.
Before the murder, to win political support, you exchanged secret letters with nobles who, like you, kept a wary eye on Macbeth.
You hold half of a secret letter.
The guard who was slain was your own man—and this puts you in a very difficult position.

You thought back to your father's words at court, and in your room you wrote a diary full of resentment about your quarrels with him.

story: You are a loyal noble—and an avenger of justice.
Years ago, your father stood against Duncan in a rebellion. It was crushed by Macbeth and Banquo, and your father was put to death by Duncan's own order.

To show a king's 'mercy' and to keep the House of Fife calm, Duncan pardoned you and let you inherit the title. Yet in your eyes, the revenge you seek for your father's death and the fear of being purged someday have never faded.
You hold half of a secret letter—one you exchanged with an important figure.
You must carefully test who is worth trusting, prove your loyalty before him, and never reveal your ultimate secret too soon.
